note: NO ITEM TEXT SHIPPED. mapping_basis/text_source describe the would-be basis only. BLOCKED on rights (irw#1945 test: the clause RESERVES A RIGHT). The RUTIIQ is developed and distributed by PARED Insights (the developers' own distributor), which requires a licence for any research or clinical use and reserves licensing costs outside academic/non-commercial use: 'Need a licence for your research or clinical practice? Complete our licence request form, and our licensing team will be in touch with further details on how you can use our UTI assessment tools in your work. For most academic research and non-commercial uses, standard user licences are available at no cost. We will advise on any licensing costs based on the details provided in the request form.' -- PARED Insights, https://paredinsights.org/assessment-tools/rutiiq/ (fetched 2026-09-19, sha256 e775d48386f3727f3d0712c583f2d92b8fce153bafb0506ea51d1200fdaec9b5); the same page states 'Upon completion of a licence for the RUTIIQ, administrators will be provided with scoring and administration instructions' and 'A full scoring guide and calculation tool are available upon completion of a licence.' A licence requirement plus a commercial fee is permission-required + fee-reserved; IRW redistributes to users whose use it cannot condition, so the free academic licence is no defence. The wording IRW would ship is the 42-item PILOT pool (a precursor of the licensed instrument, same originators), printed in the CC BY 4.0 paper's Online Resource 5 and the OSF codebook -- a CC BY reproduction does not launder a restricted instrument (ruled 2026-09-08). No instrument_rights_register.csv row existed for the RUTIIQ; this round did not write one (orchestrator may add a 'block' row). The block does achieve something: live item codes are rutiiq_a1..f10, not wording. RETRY TEST: NO -- determinate (the rights holder's licence terms bar redistribution without a licence); an unchanged retry cannot change it. What would change it: a ruling from Ben that this clause does not block, or a written grant from PARED Insights / the authors (Newlands & Finlay) permitting redistribution of the pilot item wording. BANKED FOR AN UNBLOCK (nothing else needs re-deriving): ground truth 42 items rutiiq_{a1-a6,b1-b10,c1-c8,d1-d4,e1-e4,f1-f10}, resp 0-10, n=346 per item (d 268, e 166; 240 baseline + 106 retest). Code derivation: data/uti_newlands_2023.py regex rutiiq{wave}_{suffix} -> rutiiq_{suffix}, number-preserving; the OSF 'Pilot Data Codebook.xlsx' (osf.io/download/c2984) labels every rutiiq1_/rutiiq2_ column with its item text (data_labels; _d_check/_e_check gate questions are excluded by the script). Pilot section prompts/intro verbatim in Online Resource 5 (MOESM5) phase-2 tables (sections A-F = code letters a-f). Checks run on the OSF raw file (baseline n=240): the five published subscale totals in Online Resource 11 reproduce exactly from the codebook's code->item mapping (personal a1-a4 26.18/11.08 vs 26.2/11.1; social b4,b5,b8,b9,b10 23.32/15.91 vs 23.3/15.9; work c1-c7 35.80/23.09 vs 35.8/23.1; sexual d1-d4 n=183 36.23/6.30 vs 36.2/6.3; satisfaction f1-f10 36.61/28.47 vs 36.6/28.5); stored satisfaction items are raw agreement (f-sum vs PHQ-9 Spearman -0.259, the paper's reverse-scored subscale reports +.26). SOURCE CONFLICT to resolve if unblocked: codebook gives 0=strongly disagree..10=strongly agree for e3/e4, but MOESM5 (pilot form) gives e3/e4 as SEVERITY items (0 = not present; 1 = very mild; 10 = extremely severe) under 'please indicate how SEVERE it was'; the codebook's e3/e4 labels are an editorial parenthetical, so MOESM5 is the better source there. Minor codebook vs MOESM5 wording variants: b5 'anyone' vs 'others', c1/c3 'I regularly' vs 'I have regularly', d1 'worsening UTI' vs 'worsening of UTI', d3 'relationship(s)' vs 'relationships', e1/e2 codebook full sentence vs MOESM5 'I have experienced pain or discomfort there during/within...'. note: MAPPING (paper_order): item = 'wpai_' + suffix of source column wpai{wave}_{k} (data/uti_newlands_2023.py regex; number-preserving; waves 1=baseline, 2=24h retest pooled). Neither the paper, its supplements, nor the OSF codebook ties wpai_k to wording, so wpai_k = WPAI:SHP question k rests on the form's numbering; checked in Step 5b and VERIFIED (see verification file): skip pattern (wpai_1=0 -> 2-5 absent, 84/84; =1 -> all present, 156/156; wpai_6 asked of all 240), wpai_6*10 reproduces % activity impairment (45.71/29.55 vs 45.7/29.6), wpai_4 has the only work-week-sized mean (28.9 h), wpai_2 vs wpai_3 separated by OWI SD (33.34 vs published 33.3; swap gives 31.02) and by correlation with wpai_5 (+0.44 vs -0.07). TEXT (canonical_instrument): the study adapted the WPAI:SHP to UTI (the holder instructs replacing PROBLEM with the condition name) but its adapted wording is not published anywhere in the paper, supplements or deposit, so the holder's own template is shipped verbatim with the literal placeholder PROBLEM kept (not guessed as 'UTI'/'recurrent UTI'). Version: V2.0 (the holder's current form, which repeats the instructions above the Q5/Q6 scales); the paper does not say which version was used. Wording from the printable .doc, which differs slightly from the HTML page ('your PROBLEM', 'childcare'). DEVIATIONS: the paper-form line 'Please fill in the blanks or circle a number, as indicated.', the routing lines 'If NO, check "NO" and skip to question 6.' and '(If "0", skip to question 6.)', the '_____ HOURS' answer blanks and 'CIRCLE A NUMBER' were omitted (online REDCap administration; routing is visible in the data); Q5/Q6 body paragraphs joined into item_text with the form's double spacing; 'The next questions are about the past seven days, not including today.' is section_prompt for wpai_2..6 (section _2), since the form places it after Q1. OPTIONS: wpai_1 0=NO, 1=YES (pinned by the skip pattern); wpai_5/6 0 and 10 carry the form's end anchors, 1-9 blank (unlabelled on the form); direction pinned by the activity score (reversed would give M 54.29). wpai_2/3/4 are free-entry hours: one row per observed value with blank option_text (the SelfEff/VAS precedent). DATA NOTE: 12 baseline (7 retest) employed respondents reported 0 hours worked yet answered wpai_5, which the form says to skip; REDCap did not enforce it. English administration (UK online study), so no language/_translated columns. RIGHTS (ship-shaped; register row NOT written, per the rule that rounds may not write ship rows -- escalate): WPAI_General.html item 2 'Written permission is neither required nor provided to researchers using the WPAI; there are no fees to use the WPAI or the translations on this website.' Item 3 'Modifying questionnaire wording: The questionnaire cannot be called the WPAI if questions or responses are changed or questions are added or deleted.' Judged a naming/integrity condition, not a reserved right over the wording: items 4-5 of the same page expressly permit adapting (disease name) and reformatting, so it bars neither modification nor redistribution -- it only withholds the WPAI name from altered versions; IRW ships the unaltered template. Distinct from the FATCOD register row, whose clause forbids alteration outright. Item 4 also carries a fitness caution ('Users are cautioned that although the discriminative validity and reproducibility of the specific health problem (SHP) version has been established, evidence for evaluative validity and responsiveness to clinically meaningful change has only been established for a few diseases'), which disclaims fitness and does not block (LOT-R ruling). No NC, ND, fee, permission or redistribution term located. If Ben reads item 3 as a reservation, block and withdraw.
